subject: POC Trial: Model selection and evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC Trial: Model selection and evaluation plan

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC trial so we have alignment before kickoff:

1) High-level goal
- Validate model selection and config for AvaSoft's multilingual customer support assistant (English + Spanish), prioritizing accuracy on intent extraction, low hallucination, and SLA-friendly latency.

2) Proposed success criteria (first pass)
- Intent classification / routing accuracy >= 92% on labeled test set
- Spanish parity: Spanish accuracy within 5% of English
- Hallucination rate < 2% on targeted knowledge-check set
- Latency: p95 < 500ms for typical queries (50–150 tokens)
- Cost target: average inference cost <= $0.02 per query across workloads

3) Model plan
- Primary candidate: Mistral-7B-Instruct (4-bit quantized) — chosen for strong cost/quality tradeoff and reasonable Spanish coverage.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat (full-precision or 8-bit) — used for edge cases where more context/longer responses or slightly higher accuracy is needed.
- Multilingual checks: run a small baseline with BLOOMZ-1b or bilingual checkpoints if we see gap in Spanish coverage.

4) Evaluation approach
- Two-stage: automated metrics (intent accuracy, embedding similarity for semantic match, ROUGE/ROUGE-L for specific generation tasks) + curated human eval for hallucination checks.
- Dataset: customer-provided 1k examples (balanced EN/ES) + 300 manually annotated edge cases.
- Baselines: run both candidate models under same prompt templates and temperature settings; compare latency/cost and quality.

5) Ownership & timeline
- Sales lead: Ben Carter (I'll coordinate admin, credits, and kickoff)
- Customer success / Onboarding: Laura Bennett (kickoff, credentials, workspace access)
- ML lead: Marissa Cole (evaluation plan, runs, metrics)
- Proposed timeline: environment & data prep by Nov 17; baseline runs Nov 18–24; customer review Nov 29; iterate; final report by Dec 10; target POC completion Dec 15.

6) Next steps
- I attached a draft success criteria spreadsheet and a short eval plan (see attachments). Please confirm dataset availability and whether PII/sensitive data will be included. Also confirm that the Dec 15 completion target works for you.

Thanks — I'll schedule a 30m kickoff for Friday if that works.

— Ben

- Spanish support is important; we have a ~30% Spanish volume on support channels.
- We will provide an initial 1k example dataset by EOD Nov 16, redacted for PII where possible. There will still be some legal-sensitive snippets (customer names/addresses) in edge cases — can you confirm encryption at rest and access controls for the POC workspace?

Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection and evaluation plan

Hi Sara — thanks for the questions. Quick technical notes and a more detailed eval plan attached.

1) Security / deployment
- Dedicated capacity (reserved VMs/GPU pool) is available for trials; we can provision a short-term Dedicated instance for the POC so customer data never touches the shared hosted cluster. That satisfies encryption/access controls and is SOC 2-friendly. Laura will coordinate the provisioning and contract addendum.

2) Evaluation dataset & metrics
- Recommended split: 1k examples (provided by AvaSoft) -> 800 train/dev mix for prompt tuning; 200 held-out test (100 EN / 100 ES) + 300 curated edge cases for hallucination tests.
- Metrics: intent accuracy (micro / macro), slot extraction F1 where applicable, embedding-similarity (cosine) threshold 0.85 for semantic match, ROUGE-L for templated responses, plus a human-eval checklist for hallucinations.

3) Model configs to test
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (4-bit quantized) — default temp 0.0–0.2, max_tokens per reply 256. Good first-pass baseline (fast & cost-effective).
- Llama-2-13B-chat (8-bit quantized) — higher memory and compute, expected better on complex multi-turn context; keep temperature 0.0 for deterministic routing tasks.
- If we see Spanish gaps, we'll add a bilingual model run (BLOOMZ or a multilingual fine-tune) as a third leg.

4) Ops notes (for bench runs)
- Use prefix/KV cache for multi-turn sessions in evaluation to mirror production.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency under a 20 qps shape and with batching disabled for latency-critical routes.
- Capture token counts per request to estimate cost.

5) Timeline (detailed)
- Nov 16: receive dataset (AvaSoft supplies)
- Nov 17: Dedicated instance provisioned; data ingest verified
- Nov 18–24: baseline runs for both models (EN + ES)
- Nov 25–27: human eval on top failure cases; tune prompts
- Nov 29: review call to share intermediate results
- Dec 1–8: iterate and finalize report
- Dec 10: delivery of final POC report; target POC signoff by Dec 15.

I've attached the full model-eval-plan.md with run commands, config snippets, and expected deliverables. Let me know if you want us to exclude any corpus with sensitive data from automated runs — we can do manual-only evaluation for those rows.

— Marissa
